newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government, military set for meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government, military set for meeting.

text.p: Turkey's military brass will gather with the political leadership on Friday for a meeting expected to focus on tensions between secularists and the Islamist-led government.
The National Security Council, chaired by President Suleyman Demirel and grouping senior commanders and ministers, is due to meet at 1300 GMT, the Anatolian news agency said.
Political analysts expect the council to issue a warning to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan that mounting Islamist zeal threatens Turkey's secular and democratic institutions.

Ahead of the meeting, the Turkish media carried reports of a letter -- dismissed as untrue by Erbakan and President Suleyman Demirel's office -- that Demirel had warned the Islamist-led coalition against threatening Turkey's "secularist, democratic (and) republican aims".
The government this week survived a censure motion challenge from two leftist parties who said the coalition was a threat to the country's secularism.
